dragon.title: Goodbye, Dragon Inn / 不散
dragon.event: One confirmed screening; tickets on sale
dragon.text: Tsai turns a nearly empty movie palace into a chamber of longing, cruising and collective memory. This single MoMI date is the week’s cleanest direct-focus occasion: see it tonight rather than counting on another repertory return.

sealed.title: The Sealed Soil / Khak-e Sar Be Mohr
sealed.when: Fri Oct 30 · 5:00 PM; Thu Nov 5 · 7:15 PM
sealed.text: The earliest complete surviving feature by an Iranian woman turns resistance to forced marriage into a restrained critique of institutional misogyny. Its rarity, restoration and West Asian focus make it a stronger discovery than the week’s many familiar classics.

taste.title: Taste of Cherry / طعم گیلاس
taste.event: Cinema Tehran presentation; tickets on sale
taste.text: Kiarostami’s Palme d’Or winner turns a drive through Tehran’s outskirts into a radical test of spectatorship and the ethics of representation. You have moved Life, and Nothing More… above it personally, but this rare one-night NYC booking still deserves priority.

yiyi.title: Yi Yi / 一一
yiyi.event: One public showtime in the current schedule; tickets on sale
yiyi.text: Yang’s panoramic family portrait remains one of the central works of twenty-first-century cinema, balancing social systems with small gestures and moral uncertainty. The inconvenient matinee is still worth surfacing because it is a direct-focus title with only one listed show this week.

yousee.title: You Can See Everything
yousee.event: Extended daily run; tickets on sale
yousee.text: This is the personal benchmark you identified: a public controversy routed through performance, consent, manipulation and the unstable boundary between documentary and fabrication. It is absolutely a focus film; the dense daily schedule lets you fit it around rarer one-offs rather than treating it as scarce.

queen.title: Queen at Sea
queen.when: Daily Oct 30–Nov 5; Q&A Fri Oct 30 · 7:30 PM
queen.event: Lance Hammer Q&A tonight; normal sessions eligible only if shown in MUBI GO app
queen.text: Hammer refuses easy answers around dementia, autonomy, care and who has authority to speak for another person. Use the GO ticket for a normal session; the Q&A is the better event but MUBI GO terms exclude Q&As, so buy that separately if the conversation matters.

samurai.title: The Samurai and the Prisoner / 黒牢城
samurai.event: Contenders; tickets released, live inventory / standby rules on official page
samurai.text: Kurosawa’s first chanbara replaces supernatural dread with shifting power, confinement and nested motives. It is not on the named-director list, but its Cannes-premiere status and single MoMA date make it a strong festival-to-NYC discovery.

rites.title: The Rites of May / Itim
rites.when: Mon Nov 2 · 7:00 PM; Wed Nov 4 · 9:00 PM
rites.text: De Leon folds a ghost story into the wounds of Philippine history, with transgressive imagery and a mystery of disappearance. The restoration and two-show engagement make it a high-signal cult discovery, though Monday conflicts directly with Taste of Cherry and Samurai.

devils.title: The Devils
devils.when: Daily Oct 30–Nov 5 · 4:00 & 8:30 PM (opening-day times; see live listing)
devils.event: Full uncensored restoration; limited one-week return
devils.text: Russell’s long-suppressed collision of religious power, desire and spectacle finally plays in its full form on a new 35mm print. The weeklong run lowers urgency, but the format and restored cut make this a definitive big-screen occasion.

who.title: Who Killed Alex Odeh?
who.when: Daily Oct 30–Nov 5; Q&As Fri 7:20 PM, Sat 3:00 & 5:10 PM, Sun 5:15 PM
who.event: Jason Osder Fri/Sat; Daniel Chalfen & Dawne Langford Sun; moderators listed below
who.text: A renewed investigation into the 1985 assassination of Palestinian American activist Alex Odeh connects archival evidence to unfinished political violence. Choose a guest-bearing session: the different filmmakers, producers and moderators make these meaningfully distinct events.

autumn.title: An Autumn Afternoon / 秋刀魚の味
autumn.event: One listed showtime; tickets on sale
autumn.text: Ozu’s final film turns parental duty and loneliness into a quietly devastating study of letting go. It is a canonical preference match, though the direct-focus one-offs above are harder to replace this week.

birds.title: Birds of War
birds.text: Thirteen years of archives link reporting, revolution, exile and an unexpected relationship. The subjects are also the filmmakers, making opening night a particularly substantive conversation.
birds.event: Janay Boulos & Abd Alkader Habak Q&A; tickets on sale

lagradiva.title: La Gradiva
lagradiva.event: Conversation with Marine Atlan; tickets released, live inventory / standby on official page
lagradiva.text: Atlan’s debut follows students through Naples and Pompeii as art, class, gender and desire unsettle the group. The director conversation is the reason to prioritize this MoMA session over a future regular run.

wildhorse.title: Wild Horse Nine
wildhorse.event: Conversation with Martin McDonagh, Steve Buscemi & John Malkovich; high-demand notice; standby one hour before if sold out
wildhorse.text: The guest list makes this the week’s most obvious celebrity-bearing event, and MoMA explicitly warns that Contenders capacity is extremely limited. Buy now if live inventory remains; otherwise use only MoMA’s official standby line rather than resale.

gentle.title: Gentle Monster
gentle.when: Opens Fri Oct 30; open-caption shows Sat 3:45, Sun 6:20, Mon 3:45, Tue 6:20
gentle.text: Kreutzer uses suspicion around an alleged act to test trust inside a family, carried by Léa Seydoux and Catherine Deneuve. The full run makes it a flexible second-tier choice after the rarer restorations and direct-focus films.

possible.title: Possible Love / 가능한 사랑
possible.when: Daily Oct 30–Nov 5 · 1:00, 4:15 & 7:45 PM (opening-day times; see live listing)
possible.text: Lee’s class study remains a direct focus title, but you already saw it at NYFF and have a higher-value 35mm rewatch with Heartbeat planned at Paris Theater. Use this run only for scheduling flexibility.
possible.event: Extended FLC run; Nov 24 35mm + Heartbeat remains the upgrade

father.title: Fatherland
father.venue: Film at Lincoln Center / Film Forum
father.when: Daily Oct 30–Nov 5 · multiple FLC / Film Forum sessions
father.text: The Cannes Best Director winner stays in wide local circulation. Its availability makes it a low-urgency catch-up compared with the one-night focus titles and restorations.
father.event: Extended regular run; no new guest event this week

soul.title: Soul Patrol
soul.when: Sneak preview Thu Nov 5 · 7:30 PM; opens Fri Nov 6 · 7:15 PM
soul.text: The Sundance documentary directing-award winner opens with two guest-bearing shows. Harper and subject-author Ed Emanuel will discuss its archive-driven reconstruction of the first Black special-operations team in Vietnam.
soul.event: Q&As with J.M. Harper & Ed Emanuel Nov 5 at 7:30 PM and Nov 6 at 7:15 PM; tickets on sale

hamaguchi.title: All of a Sudden / Soudain
hamaguchi.when: FLC previews Nov 18–19; MoMA Nov 19 · 6:00 PM
hamaguchi.text: You already saw it at NYFF and want the guest-bearing rewatch. Prioritize whichever FLC preview has the better conversation once exact times appear; keep MoMA’s Nov 12 public sale as the confirmed fallback.
hamaguchi.event: Hamaguchi & Tao Okamoto at FLC; Hamaguchi at MoMA. MoMA public sale Nov 12, 10:30 AM ET

lantern.title: Raise the Red Lantern / 大红灯笼高高挂
lantern.text: Gong Li’s performance and Zhang’s enclosure of bodies inside ritual are essential Fifth Generation cinema. The new 35th-anniversary engagement warrants a deliberate big-screen revisit rather than a buried calendar mention.

bitter.title: Bitter Christmas
bitter.event: Tickets on sale; showtimes on official listing
bitter.text: An actress writes from other lives inside a film invented by an Almodóvar-like filmmaker. Its layered traffic between experience and fabrication makes it a good match for your new nonfiction-and-authorship interest, even though it is fiction.

everytime.title: Everytime
everytime.text: Wollner’s formally surprising grief drama won Cannes Un Certain Regard and moves directly into a short exclusive run. It is a stronger coming-week bet than waiting for a broad rollout that may not materialize.

cameron.title: Cameron Winter at Carnegie Hall
cameron.text: Anderson’s 35mm record of Winter’s sold-out Carnegie Hall performance is a compact A24 occasion with a format-specific reason to go. It belongs in the 30-day window even without a guest announcement.
